steps.content: After a night spent riding out the storm, by the time you finally arrive at the Bureau, your wound has already become severely infected.
[Scene Change] Operating room. Perhaps reuse the ceiling perspective from CH1, with Mania visual effects, red pulsing, etc.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Fever, infection, and Mania contamination?! How did you let it get this bad?!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: A wound from a Rancor weapon, and no emergency treatment at all? What were you people thinking? Even the Shattered Blade should have—

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: ...I'm sorry. Shattered Blade delayed me. I couldn't reach Chief in time.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: No... if only we'd caught up to Jasmine sooner, none of this...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I was being reckless... I put Shattered... Nirvana Port in a tough spot. They offered treatment, but I decided... I wanted to get back as soon as possible...
Staying there any longer would only put Jasmine's mental state at greater risk. She needed to be taken away from Nirvana Port as quickly as possible, away from anything that might trigger her.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I'll be fine... They patched me up enough, and my... Mania resistance is high. I can take it. Just...
Your consciousness grows hazy. The words you speak sound far away, as if they belong to someone else.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: <size=36>Just</size><size=35>...</size> <size=34>please</size> <size=33>check</size> <size=32>on</size> <size=31>Jasmine</size> <size=30>for</size> <size=29>me.</size> <size=28>I'll</size><size=27>...</size> <size=26>leave</size> <size=25>her</size> <size=24>in</size> <size=23>your</size> <size=22>hands</size><size=21>...</size>

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: You don't even need to ask! Chief, worry about yourself right now. Save your strength. We're prepping for surgery. Let me administer the—

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Stay Back!

Jasmine violently slaps the nurse's hand aside. She reacts with fierce alarm to the sharp needle coming near you, arching her back like a lioness guarding your bed, utterly oblivious to how terrified and fragile she appears.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: He went to that place and this is what happened... Those Rancors did this. Those Disian blades hurt him... Not a single good person here. No one can be trusted... Anything I have, you people just take and take and—
steps.female_content: She went to that place and this is what happened... Those Rancors did this. Those Disian blades hurt her... Not a single good person here. No one can be trusted... Anything I have, you people just take and take and—

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: STAY BACK!! Don't you dare touch him!!
steps.female_content: STAY BACK!! Don't you dare touch her!!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: What are you saying?! Chief needs surgery right now! His fever's already at 41! Do you want to watch him lose a limb?!
steps.female_content: What are you saying?! Chief needs surgery right now! Her fever's already at 41! Do you want to watch her lose a limb?!

steps.content: The words jolt through her like an electric shock. All the color drains from her face, and though no sound escapes her lips, she refuses to step back.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Jasmine...
You force out a thin, broken whisper. It reaches her.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Chief!
In an instant, she snaps back to herself, pressing close and gripping your hand. The rest of the world falls away.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Does it still hurt? Here... let me hold you. I'll draw the fever into me, then it won't burn you anymore. ...Is that a little better?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm right here. Jasmine's right here. I won't let any of them near you again, not one step closer. I won't let anything hurt you ever again. Your face is so pale... Would you take my blood? You can have all of it. Please...

Before you, Jasmine's silhouette blurs and sways like a mirage. Her eyes, flooded with tears, hold yours with an aching urgency. Hatred has been washed clean from those depths; what remains is vast, unguarded fear and sorrow. She cannot bring herself to step away, afraid that one blink is all it would take to lose someone she holds dear again.
Through you, who is she really seeing? How many beloved faces has she watched disappear in agony, ripped from her grasp one by one?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Please... say something. Just tell me what to do. Anything... please...

You ache to answer her. But the fever and the relentless pain consume you whole. Your body and mind are slowly coming undone, drifting away from each other. Your sight goes dark at the edges, and then everything fades.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Don't close your eyes. Please... please don't close your eyes... Chief!

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Get away! I told you, stay back! Mm—!
A hand grabs Jasmine and spins her around. Fury flares in her chest, ready to ignite, only to be smothered by a rebuke far sharper than the one she was about to deliver.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Enough, Jasmine! Scratching and clawing around him like that won't fix anything. Chief's practically foaming at the mouth! Here, feel this. Colder than your hands, right? If you want him to wake up, then use the fever patch. You won't let us touch him? Fine. You do it!
steps.female_content: Enough, Jasmine! Scratching and clawing around her like that won't fix anything. Chief's practically foaming at the mouth! Here, feel this. Colder than your hands, right? If you want her to wake up, then use the fever patch. You won't let us touch her? Fine. You do it!

steps.content: Something ice-cold slaps into Jasmine's palm. She flinches, and her vision clears just enough to see a familiar face. It's someone who works with ${PlayerName}. The girl grips Jasmine firmly by the shoulders, holding her steady.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: I know you understand me, Jasmine. You're not actually a cat. You're smart. So listen. Really listen! This wound would've killed any desert bandit by now, and Chief's in worse shape than they are. That field first aid of yours won't save him.
steps.female_content: I know you understand me, Jasmine. You're not actually a cat. You're smart. So listen. Really listen! This wound would've killed any desert bandit by now, and Chief's in worse shape than they are. That field first aid of yours won't save her.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: He needs surgery. Surgery. You know what that means? A whole team working on him, real experts. And we are running out of time! So you are going to help, right now!
steps.female_content: She needs surgery. Surgery. You know what that means? A whole team working on her, real experts. And we are running out of time! So you are going to help, right now!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: You're not the only person who cares about Chief. He matters to all of us. If we waste any more time, he's going to die. And if <color=#fb9259>he dies</color>, I will <size=45>NEVER</size> <size=50>EVER</size> forgive you!
steps.female_content: You're not the only person who cares about Chief. She matters to all of us. If we waste any more time, she's going to die. And if <color=#fb9259>she dies</color>, I will <size=45>NEVER</size> <size=50>EVER</size> forgive you!

steps.content: The words hit like a thunderclap. Jasmine stands frozen, rooted to the spot. After a long silence, she speaks, her voice hollow and dry.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...He's going to die...? He won't come back? Even he will...?
steps.female_content: ...She's going to die...? She won't come back? Even she will...?

steps.content: She glances at Wynn, then at you, and suddenly all the strength drains from her body.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Sob... no... no, please... My blades. Where are my blades... Say something... Someone save him... please save him...
steps.female_content: Sob... no... no, please... My blades. Where are my blades... Say something... Someone save her... please save her...

steps.content: Whimpering, she reaches out blindly. The ice pack slips from her grasp and hits the floor, leaving her hands empty, clutching at nothing. She curls in on herself, covering her eyes, unable to look at you or draw close. Slowly, she edges backward, trying to disappear into the shadows.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: It's all my fault... What am I supposed to do...? My blades aren't here... I don't know what to do...
A flicker of panic crosses Wynn's face too. She quickly takes Jasmine's hand, then opens her arms and pulls her into a tight embrace.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: What good are those blades supposed to do? Here, I'll teach you. The doctors will handle the surgery. Your job is to hold Chief's hand. Give him strength. Help him pull through. Okay?
steps.female_content: What good are those blades supposed to do? Here, I'll teach you. The doctors will handle the surgery. Your job is to hold Chief's hand. Give her strength. Help her pull through. Okay?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Well, it's... it's not really that bad. The doctors here are amazing. Chief's body might, maybe, possibly, probably be stronger than it used to be? And more than anything... what you feel for Chief is the real miracle right there.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: ...That's all made-up TV drama stuff. Surgery requires a sterile environment. Ow!
Wynn kicks him sharply in the shin. The nurse is back too, jumping into the conversation with a huff.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: The attending physician just called. He's on his way, and he said if Jasmine wants to stay, it might actually be better. Could be a real opportunity. We just need to manage the sterilization.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: But once the surgery begins, ${PlayerName} may bleed. There could be emergencies. We can handle all of that, but it won't be easy to watch. Can you stay calm through it?

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: If you have another outburst then, you could really hurt ${PlayerName}. Can you keep yourself under control? Do you trust yourself to do that?

She turns to Jasmine, all traces of their earlier argument gone. Her gaze is steady and grave now, fixed on Jasmine's eyes. She is waiting for an answer, one that comes from a responsible human being.
[Black Screen]

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: BP, heart rate... defibrillator on standby, compression device ready, prepare for intubation...

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Is the patient still stable?
[Black Screen]

Jasmine doesn't remain inside. She makes the choice to leave the operating room herself, but she doesn't wander far. She stays just out the door, where she crouches low, her spine pressed against the seam of the doorframe.

Wynn settles an arm around her shoulders, soothing her with a low, steady voice. Eugene keeps vigil close by, relaying requests back and forth over comms—water, blankets, medicine to calm Jasmine's nerves.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: It's okay. It's going to be okay. They've handled far worse than this. He'll pull through...
steps.female_content: It's okay. It's going to be okay. They've handled far worse than this. She'll pull through...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm sorry... I'm really sorry...
The Rancor is gone. Her hands can no longer grip the blades. This time, someone else reaches for her icy fingers instead, gripping them hard, holding on with all their strength.
(Surgery Sound: Beep————)
[Black Screen]

Three Days
After Returning the Rancor

You open your eyes. The surgery is behind you now, with no surprises, no complications, a success as assured as the sunrise. You even managed a few untroubled dreams, the first in what feels like forever.
The visitors are many. FAC veterans, the Bureau's youngest Sinners, even friends with their pets in tow. You have seen a whole spectrum of people, one after another.
It wears on you a little, if you're honest. But every single visit is rooted in pure goodwill, so you welcome them all without complaint.
You hope, more than anything, that Jasmine sees it, that she can feel even a fraction of that warmth.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: We're still trying not to trigger her. While you've been out, Jasmine's had Wynn and the others keeping her company. She's talking to a few people now, even expressing her needs on her own... She's working on reconnecting. It's a world apart from where she was.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: She actually asked for more treatment options. Said she wants to get better faster... Whatever you call it, she's searching for ways to quiet the pain that don't involve revenge. And she's stopped pushing everyone away.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: You did it, Chief. That's no small thing.
...Did I?
You glance back. Jasmine is there, tucked into the corner of the sofa. She's drawn up so small, so tight, until her eyes find yours.
Eyes meeting, no words spoken yet, she gets to her feet. And then she comes to you, compliant, as if drawn by an invisible thread.
[Black Screen Transition]

One Week
After Returning the Rancor

One by one, the promises between the two of you are being kept. Sunbathing in an Eastside park, visiting hidden-gem eateries deep in the alleyways, catching glimpses of what the Outlands settlement streets look like from a distance. She says she's happy, but she always keeps herself a little apart. Perhaps she still can't quite handle being around crowds.

Every time Wynn returns from a shopping trip, she brings Jasmine clothes and accessories, insisting that now she's put down the blades, Jasmine ought to look her best. Jasmine only picks out a soft silk loungewear top. She slips it on, rubs the fabric against her cheek, and smiles, saying she really loves it. She knows exactly how to make Wynn happy.

Most of the time, she stays in your office while you work, keeping you company. She no longer acts out for attention, no longer stirs up mischief. She's friendly and polite to everyone now. She doesn't push water glasses off your desk anymore, doesn't sneak glances at your terminal or files.

She still wakes in the middle of the night, haunted by nightmares, but when you call her name, she no longer struggles or tries to flee. She makes an effort to stay within your sight and calm herself down. The next day, she seeks out the doctor for treatment on her own.
The words she says to you most often are:
...Alright. I'll do as you say.
All of the hatred and the self-destructive pulse seem to have been wiped away, as if by someone's hand. Yet you find it hard to feel any relief.
You know the wounds are far from healed.

Two Months
After Returning the Rancor
[Bureau, alarm blaring, panicked shouting]
The alarm blares without warning. People rush through the corridors, searching for someone. You step out and stop a nurse.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I'm not entirely sure. Jasmine said she wanted to spend some time with other Sinners, so I brought her over. It was going fine at first... everyone chatting and laughing.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Then EMP got excited and said she wanted to throw a welcome party, a little event. She asked Jasmine to dance... and then suddenly, this.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...A "celebration."
You rush out immediately.
Through the swirling chaos, you trace the shackles' pull until you arrive, alone, at an empty warehouse.
No answer comes from the darkness. You know she's there, but flipping on the lights too abruptly might trigger her. You decide to try a different approach.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That's strange. The shackles are pointing straight here, but nobody's around... Is she up high? I can't reach the shelves unless I stretch... let me just—

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Ah—ow, ow, ow...
A figure darts to your side in a flash, seizing your hand to check the old wound, only for you to catch her in return.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Got you.
A tremor runs through her, yet she can't bring herself to fight or flee. She simply stays still in your grip, her body folding inward, shrinking.
The damp chill of her palms meets your fingers. Something tightens in your chest, and regret washes over you all at once.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...I'm sorry. It was meant to be a joke. I didn't mean to frighten you.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I'm fine. You've been taking such good care of me. I was just worried.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Are you okay, Jasmine? What happened back there...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm good...
After a moment, she goes on.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm sorry... I've caused trouble for you again. They mentioned a celebration, and I just...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: No... it's not the celebration. It's not that. I'll try. I'll try harder. I'll get over this. I'll keep moving forward, I promise...

She lowers her head even further, her hands scratching at her skin uncontrollably. The dim corridor light catches scars both new and old. She scratches hard as if punishing herself, or perhaps holding something back.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Take me to the doctor... You can freeze me if you want. I don't need to wake up again... I don't want to cause any more trouble. I can't... keep going like this...
You can't find the words. Instead, you take her hand and press it firmly into your palm. A long moment passes before you force yourself to speak, the words coming out strained.
You know the truth: nothing you offer can mend what came before. She's simply remembering what it feels like to lose.

Fear swallows everything else. It's what made her let go of hatred, and what now makes her bury it inside herself, sharp edge turned inward. You've only dug deeper, uncovering wounds she'd hidden even from herself.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: This is just a small injury. I'm not going to die. And none of it is your fault. I didn't think it through. I never should have let you see something like that again.
You want to tell her you regret it.

The pain is a massive, roaring thing inside her. It howls for an exit, but finds none. And so, rather than watch her bury it deeper into herself, you'd rather she turn that blade on the world outside, let her hate the cruelty of it all, or let her hate you.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: If you're angry, then yell at me. Hit me if you have to. Lie to me, use me, manipulate me... I don't care. Throw all of it at me. I can take it.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...I'll be here. I'm not going anywhere.
She gazes at you, lost in a daze. The sealed chamber of her heart cracks open again at last, yet what escapes is a flood of bewilderment, fear, and restless doubt.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...You... Why are you so kind to me?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You could've just let me go. You should've left me alone. Why do you keep holding on? If you hadn't followed me that day, I never would have—

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Even if I died, it wouldn't have anything to do with you...
You remember it clearly. Just a few months ago, inside that interrogation room, when the air between you was still charged with friction, she asked you much the same question.
...That's right. Why? When did it all begin?
You hold Jasmine's gaze, and the nightmares flash before your eyes. Fear, rage, hatred, madness, the helplessness of loss, the agony of powerlessness...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...We're the same...
[CG Flash: Hella suffering in war]

You can bury them again and again, but seeing Jasmine always pulls them back to the surface. They stitch themselves into fresh nightmares, whispering the same truth: the war was real. It crushed everything in its path. This chapter cannot be erased.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You're lying... You're a Disian...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You're a Disian... and you're telling me we... are the same?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You're right. I spoke out of turn. I'm sorry.
Gently, you pull her into your arms.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: We're not the same. But I have pain I can't shoulder alone either. Wounds I can't heal by myself. That's why I want you to get better.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: People heal others to heal themselves. Walk beside someone long enough, and somehow, you end up moving forward too. Like right now...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Holding you through this... it feels like someone's holding me, too.
Her expression is hidden from you. A long stillness stretches between you before she finally speaks, her voice barely above a whisper.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Can it really be healed?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I don't know, Jasmine. I don't know...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: But if it ever hurts too much, if you can't take it alone anymore... then give some of it to me...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: As long as you're alive. As long as you still want to be. Even if the road ahead is nothing but wasteland... someone will walk it with you, waiting for the flowers to grow back...
Does she understand? You don't know.
All you feel is a pair of trembling hands climbing up to your shoulders. And then...
...She holds on tight.
[Black Screen Transition]

A Long Time
After Returning the Rancor

So much has happened since then, both good and bad. Jasmine has long settled into her own room by now, the one filled with plushes from Wynn, and a little cat she's taken in. She no longer needs you there every night to feel safe.
So tonight, when she shows up at your bedside, fully dressed, quietly waiting for you to wake, it surprises you.
Once you're sure this isn't a dream, you reach out and take her hand.

options: Did you have a nightmare? Are you alright?

choices.text: Did you have a nightmare? Are you alright?

steps.content: Her hand isn't as cold as before, but she still seems dazed. It takes a long while for her to speak.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I... had a dream.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I dreamed I was on stage... and I had to dance. A different kind of dance.
Her gaze is far away. Her words come so very slow.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: No blades to hold. No cannons... I was at another celebration. It felt familiar, but strange too. So many eyes on me... family, guests, strangers... You were there as well, sitting with the Disians, waiting for me to dance...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: But it's been so long... I've forgotten how to dance without those blades in my hands... If I stepped onto that stage now, everyone would just laugh...
A long pause. Then Jasmine lifts her eyes to yours, hesitant and uncertain.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Would you... watch me? Just... think of it as practice?
Jasmine holds your gaze as she retreats, step by slow step, to the very center of the room.

The night light is pale and thin. If you let your eyes blur, it could be moonlight slanting in, a bonfire's glow that holds the two of you within its quiet circle. Her hands rise upward, as though greeting the sky itself. Her body, soft and fluid, moves like a stream catching the moon's rippling shimmer.

There are no blades, no bloodshed, only an audience of one. The dancer closes her eyes, following a beat no one else can hear, searching through the splinters of memory to gather back the steps she thought she'd lost.
Through wind, through dust, across impossible distances, she journeys on until she reaches the buried end of time.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Let flame ignite the candles bright, to greet the seedlings in the light.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Let arrows fly to strike the mark, to hear what a grandmother's blessings impart.
[Switch Scene]

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Chief, a confidential letter for you. It's from the farlands.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It was routed through internal channels, so security isn't an issue. But... yes, no signature.
It's not really a letter. There's no message inside. The sender seems to have nothing to say to you.
Or perhaps they believe you'll understand without needing words.
You look down at the "letter" in your hand.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...Notify Outland Affairs and the 9th Agency. Tell them they can call off the search.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I know where it is. I'll find a time to go myself...
[DisCity Night View]

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Let parades roll through fields so wide, and drift into sweet dreams inside. Let fireworks gleam in skies above, illuminating homes built with love.
[Scene Change: Nirvana Port]

The general of DisCity returns from another far-flung expedition. The city-state's newest war proposal goes straight into the trash, discarded without ceremony, before she makes her way back to the cemetery beyond Nirvana Port.
Dozens of new headstones have sprung up across the burial ground. Some were raised over bones she carried home herself. Others mark fresh graves, dug in the aftermath of the latest conflict.

She finds the stone bearing Arkin's name. The ones lined up beside it belong to the same group of fools who followed him into the fire. She couldn't bring them back. Maybe they wouldn't have wanted her to. Maybe they'd even call it a decent way to go.
The general gazes at them for a long, long time. Then she walks up and gives each grave a solid, brutal kick.
After that, she crouches down and leaves a few belated photographs at Arkin's grave.
[Outlands Outskirts] Apply photo/print filter
In those photos, past windswept sands, across a thousand miles, at the buried end of all things lies a valley. A battlefield long forgotten.

The years have worn everything down. Homes, fields, craters, bones... The lost village is nothing now but scattered rubble. No one ever raised a monument. Perhaps the photographer thought it would ring hollow.

So instead, she carried a pair of blades to this place—nearly shattered, barely holding together—and planted them among the ruins, at the best vantage point in the whole ruins. If there were ever celebrations here, this would have been center stage.
The blades stand there now, center stage. And then...
[Background continues, remove photo/print filter, apply dreamlike, hallucinatory filter]

From the dust, green shoots emerge. They follow the cracks along the steel, climbing, reaching upward. A new bud trembles on the verge of blooming, and it almost catches the echo of joyful voices cheering from below the stage.

steps.speaker: Villager A
steps.content: Jasmine... Jasmine...

steps.speaker: Villager B
steps.content: The celebration is right around the corner! Harvest came in full this year. And those guests from way back have come around again...

steps.speaker: Villager B
steps.content: They still remember the celebration. They remember your dancing... And they brought gifts, too. Said they've been meaning to return the kindness all this time.

steps.speaker: Villager C
steps.content: They brought gifts? Well, that makes them our friends!

The flowers bloom. Green leaves spill over the stage, burying the shattered Rancor blades, washing the devastation clean. Perhaps the fires of war never truly ignited. Sunlight breaks through the sandstorm once more, and face after face emerges through the calamity to join the celebration.

People wipe the blood from their faces. They throw their blades aside and embrace with wild laughter, drink deep, dance together, shouting at the top of their lungs in their mother tongue and in Disian:

steps.speaker: Villager C
steps.content: Come on, Jasmine! The celebration is starting!
[Office]
The dance ends without warning. There is no smile, no graceful bow, only a puppet whose strings have been severed. She stands hollow, adrift, in the dim room of a foreign land.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: It's over...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: When the celebration ends... there's really nothing left at all...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: There's nothing left, Chief... None of it can ever come back...
Wordless, you step forward and gather her into your arms.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That was a wonderful celebration. I will never forget it.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: None of us will...
Slowly, you feel dampness spread across your chest. Soft sobs reach your ears, and then at last, she breaks into full, unrestrained weeping.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Aah... aaaaaah...

Through the battlefields, through the nightmares, torn open by hatred and terror, the celebration, frozen in time, has at last reached its end. So much was stolen from her. She has been chasing it for so long. And now, only now, does she take the first step, recovering the first treasure she lost so long ago.
You hold her close, as tightly as you can.
The one who lost her home finally sheds her broken smile and finds her tears again. Her heart, stitched together from fragments, remembers how to grieve at last.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: O traveler, when you join a celebration in a foreign land...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Brush the dust from your sleeves, raise your cup high. Let us toast this meeting. Let us savor this night. And before you depart, full of good cheer, look forward to the year ahead.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Another year... and another after that. Dear friends from afar... may we gather again.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: At the next celebration, may I find you there.
